entries.name: Temporal restricted Boltzmann machine
entries.definition: A neural sequence architecture that multiplies time-indexed conditional RBM distributions whose visible and hidden biases depend on preceding visible and hidden states through shared temporal weights.
entries.identity_notes: This record covers the original single-layer temporal RBM construction of Sutskever and Hinton, with its finite lag window and omitted-edge special cases. The full architecture has visible-to-visible, visible-to-hidden and hidden-to-hidden history connections. It is distinct from temporal FRBM’s factored categorical-word construction, RTRBM’s deterministic recurrent state, and the observed-history-only autoregressive CRBM. Multilayer stacking is an extension rather than part of this single-layer identity; a filtering algorithm does not define the latent probabilistic model. limitations: The conditional partition depends on history, including previous hidden states. It is not one sequence-independent global constant, and exact posterior Gibbs updates can require ratios of such partitions.

A factorial posterior given known latent history does not imply factorial or exact filtering after uncertain history is marginalized. Mean substitution through nonlinear normalized factors is generally approximate, and future observations can revise earlier hidden-state posteriors.

The paper explicitly notes that changing its parameter-dependent approximate posterior can reduce the variational bound. Finite CD, mean visible reconstructions and ignoring future evidence provide no monotonic bound or likelihood guarantee.

TRBM-HH denotes the variant with hidden-to-hidden links omitted, not one retaining only those links. For fully observed visible sequences its hidden posterior is factorial; missing observations and multilayer compositions change that inference problem.

The displayed construction has no past-hidden-to-current-visible links; a footnote mentions those as a possible extension. Gaussian visible units, deeper compositions and different lag structures require their own stated assumptions. No empirical ranking, long-memory guarantee or author-code behavior is certified.

claims.statement: For binary vectors v_t and h_t, set the visible bias a_t=a+sum_k A_k^T v_(t-k) and hidden bias b_t=b+sum_k B_k^T h_(t-k)+sum_k C_k^T v_(t-k). Define p(v_t,h_t|history)=exp(v_t^T C_0 h_t+a_t^T v_t+b_t^T h_t)/Z_t(history), and multiply these normalized factors over time using shared parameters and the source’s learned initial contributions for unavailable earlier states. Conditional on observed current and previous visibles and known previous hidden states, the current hidden posterior factorizes with probabilities sigmoid(C_0^T v_t+b_t). Unknown previous hidden states generally require marginalization; the proposed online filter instead substitutes their inferred probability vectors in b_t. Learning treats these approximate filtered states as context and uses per-step contrastive-divergence updates. The original paper distinguishes this approximation from smoothing with future observations and from an exact likelihood gradient.

entries.name: Recurrent temporal restricted Boltzmann machine
entries.definition: A recurrent neural sequence architecture whose deterministic state is a conditional RBM hidden-probability vector and sets the next step’s hidden bias, with visible observations drawn from that step’s RBM marginal.
entries.identity_notes: This is Sutskever, Hinton and Taylor’s 2008 RTRBM, with a real-valued recurrent state and separate binary within-step RBM hidden variables. Replacing a sampled TRBM hidden state by a deterministic probability vector changes the generative model; exact inference in RTRBM is not exact inference in the original stochastic TRBM. limitations: Exact deterministic-state inference requires the visible sequence to be observed. Missing observations require marginalizing uncertainty in visible values and induced recurrent states; the exact-inference statement does not automatically extend to that problem.

Within-step binary hidden variables are stochastic even though the recurrent summary is deterministic. Exact state reconstruction does not make RBM partition functions, equilibrium sampling or finite-CD gradients exact or generally tractable.

The printed Equation (12) local-score index differs from its surrounding next-step prose. Equation (13) displays a recurrence contribution but omits the direct current-RBM dependence through its dynamic hidden bias; a complete objective derivative must include it. The curated description follows the normalized generative definition and chain rule, checked by original finite differences, rather than treating Equations (12)–(14) as a verified implementation. No author-code defect or official erratum is asserted.

A finite recurrent vector permits temporal dependence but does not guarantee successful learning of arbitrarily long dependencies. The source’s sample-quality comparisons do not establish universal superiority or exact likelihood learning.

The source shares parameters between recurrence and output RBMs. A separate recurrent network that independently controls RBM parameters is a distinct neighboring construction; this record does not equate every RNN–RBM hybrid to RTRBM.

claims.statement: Use column vectors, visible-by-hidden weights W and recurrent hidden-by-hidden weights U. Given r_(t-1), let the current binary RBM have joint mass proportional to exp(v_t^T W z_t+a^T v_t+(b+U r_(t-1))^T z_t), with binary z_t marginalized for the visible distribution. After observing or sampling v_t, set r_t=sigmoid(W^T v_t+b+U r_(t-1)); the first step uses the specified initial bias contribution. This update is deterministic by definition, so a fully observed visible sequence fixes the recurrent trajectory exactly and later observations cannot alter its already determined states. The visible-sequence log likelihood is the sum of the conditional RBM log marginals. Differentiate that objective through the recurrence and through each RBM’s direct parameter dependence. In particular, a recurrent weight affects the current output distribution through its hidden bias as well as later recurrent states. Backpropagation through time propagates these dependencies, while the paper approximates conditional RBM model expectations with contrastive divergence. A Gaussian-visible version replaces the binary visible base measure with a quadratic Gaussian term.

Replacing Gaussian visible samples by conditional means removes conditional sampling variance and is not exact Gibbs sampling from the stated Gaussian model. Finite CD is not an exact likelihood gradient or a convergence guarantee.

claims.statement: Condition on preceding visible frames and compute dynamic biases d_t=c+sum_k A_k^T v_(t-k) and e_t=b+sum_k D_k^T v_(t-k), allowing different lag windows for the two sums. In the source’s unit-variance Gaussian formulation, E(v_t,h_t|history)=one-half times ||v_t-d_t|| squared minus e_t^T h_t minus v_t^T W h_t. Thus hidden probabilities are sigmoid(e_t+W^T v_t), and visible coordinates given h_t are independent unit-variance Gaussians with mean d_t+W h_t. The partition is conditional on the fixed history. For fully observed frames the hidden posterior factorizes, and likelihood gradients contrast data and conditional-model statistics; the paper approximates them by CD while holding earlier frames fixed. Its implementation description samples positive-phase binary hidden states, uses hidden probabilities for negative-phase statistics, and uses mean visible reconstructions in place of Gaussian draws. Generation starts from supplied initial frames and repeatedly samples the current conditional RBM; the original conditional training does not model the first lag-window frames.

Four complete native neighbors were inspected: static and temporal FRBM (previous full reading with byte verification), sigmoid belief network and hidden Markov model (read this batch). TRBM and autoregressive CRBM broadly map to ArtificialNeuralNetwork; RTRBM broadly maps to RecurrentNeuralNetwork through its deterministic recurrence and RBM-output objective. All three relate to RestrictedBoltzmannMachine through their within-step conditional construction. BoltzmannMachineNetwork has a symmetric whole-network scope that does not cover directed temporal links unchanged. RecurrentLayer, HiddenLayer and ProbabilisticHiddenLayer are components, not whole sequence architectures. BayesianNetwork does not identify the mixed directed/undirected parameterization, and ProbabilisticGraphicalModel is task-scoped in this pin. MarkovChain does not identify the neural parameterization; marginal visible histories and hidden/state augmentation require explicit boundaries. DeepBeliefNetwork and DeepNeuralNetwork are not implied by a single hidden layer unrolled in time. AutoregressiveLanguageModel, CausalLLM, ControllableLLM, EnergyBasedLLM and ImplicitLanguageModel require language-specific scope. VectorAutoregression is linear; AutoregressiveDistributedLag does not identify a conditional energy model. GaussianNoiseLayer is training-time regularization, not a Gaussian visible conditional, and TemporalBias is a selection/sampling bias, not a dynamic neural bias. Previous native models provide boundaries without reassessing their own scientific approval.

claims.statement: Apply shared FRBM parameters to successive overlapping word windows. Connect hidden state h_tau to h_(tau+1) so that the current hidden bias becomes b_h+A h_tau; conditional on that earlier state, the current word and hidden variables retain an FRBM joint with its own normalizer. Exact prediction must account for uncertainty in previous hidden states. The proposed online approximation instead substitutes their inferred probabilities p_tau, computes p_(tau+1)=sigmoid(b_h+A p_tau+sum_i W_i^T r_word_i) after observing the current window, and predicts the next word using the FRBM word distribution with the correspondingly shifted bias. Learning uses these approximate filtered probabilities, applies contrastive-divergence updates to individual model instances, and combines them. The temporal-weight update contrasts current hidden probabilities and their reconstruction, multiplied by the preceding filtered vector; it does not propagate an exact likelihood gradient through the full latent history.

claims.statement: Write r_w for the shared column embedding of word w. For context positions 1 through n-1 and candidate word w at position n, define t=b_h+sum_(i<n) W_i^T r_context_i+W_n^T r_w and candidate bias a_w=b_r^T r_w+b_w. The conditional joint energy is E(w,h;context)=-t^T h-a_w. Summing binary h gives unnormalized word mass exp(a_w) times product_j(1+exp(t_j)); normalize these masses over candidate words. Given all words, hidden units are independent Bernoulli with probabilities sigmoid(t_j). Given h, the next word has softmax scores r_w^T W_n h+a_w. Exact conditional likelihood gradients use data-posterior statistics minus model expectations, whose vocabulary sum is explicit. The paper instead trains latent-variable models using finite contrastive divergence: start at the observed word, update hidden, word and hidden states, and contrast resulting statistics. Some runs replace the sampled one-hot word with its probability vector, a mean-field reconstruction variant.

native_neighbors.name: Sigmoid belief network
native_neighbors.definition: A directed acyclic probabilistic network of binary variables whose forward conditional probabilities are logistic functions of weighted parent states and a bias.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is the sigmoid conditional family defined by Neal, including equivalent zero/one and minus-one/plus-one encodings. Hidden variables are permitted but not required; the fully visible autoregressive specialization is not treated as an alias for the whole family. claims.statement: Choose a topological ordering of binary nodes and directed connections from earlier parents to later nodes. In zero/one encoding let a_i=b_i+sum_j w_ij s_j over parents; then P(s_i=1|parents)=sigmoid(a_i) and P(s_i=0|parents)=1-sigmoid(a_i). Multiplying these locally normalized factors gives the joint distribution without an undirected global partition function. Ancestral sampling visits nodes in topological order. For the equivalent minus-one/plus-one encoding, divide each non-bias weight by two and add half the original incoming-weight sum to the original bias. Marginalizing hidden variables still requires a sum over their configurations, and a Gibbs full conditional uses both the node factor and factors of its children, rather than merely its forward conditional. In the inspected maximum-likelihood learning derivation, gradients of a visible-data log likelihood are posterior expectations of joint log-probability scores; Gibbs sampling is one approximation for those expectations, not a mandatory part of the architecture.

source_analysis.mapping_assessment: All 44 semantic hits and 21 exact annotated AIO CLASS nodes with outgoing edges were read. Fourteen corresponding generated YAML files were previously fully read and verified byte-identical; seven were read in this batch. Four complete native neighbors were inspected: static and temporal FRBM (previous full reading with byte verification), sigmoid belief network and hidden Markov model (read this batch). TRBM and autoregressive CRBM broadly map to ArtificialNeuralNetwork; RTRBM broadly maps to RecurrentNeuralNetwork through its deterministic recurrence and RBM-output objective. All three relate to RestrictedBoltzmannMachine through their within-step conditional construction. BoltzmannMachineNetwork has a symmetric whole-network scope that does not cover directed temporal links unchanged. RecurrentLayer, HiddenLayer and ProbabilisticHiddenLayer are components, not whole sequence architectures. BayesianNetwork does not identify the mixed directed/undirected parameterization, and ProbabilisticGraphicalModel is task-scoped in this pin. MarkovChain does not identify the neural parameterization; marginal visible histories and hidden/state augmentation require explicit boundaries. DeepBeliefNetwork and DeepNeuralNetwork are not implied by a single hidden layer unrolled in time. AutoregressiveLanguageModel, CausalLLM, ControllableLLM, EnergyBasedLLM and ImplicitLanguageModel require language-specific scope. VectorAutoregression is linear; AutoregressiveDistributedLag does not identify a conditional energy model. GaussianNoiseLayer is training-time regularization, not a Gaussian visible conditional, and TemporalBias is a selection/sampling bias, not a dynamic neural bias. Previous native models provide boundaries without reassessing their own scientific approval.
